goal: A long-lived mc process runs the code on main: the merger, the repo watcher and the runner each notice, between units of work, that the checkout has moved past the commit they started on, finish what is in flight and hand over to a successor on the new code; `mc run --update` says what each will do, and the page shows any process behind its checkout.
The merger writes what it already knows when it knows it: an answer given before a round reaches `merges.json` at once, and a mend starts as soon as the mend line is free.
A plan is done when every step is done and every success criterion is met, and the door keeps a last step from landing with a criterion unmet.
A re-plan moves a step's register state with the step, not with its slot, and every register write leaves a line saying which process made it.
contract: Steps 1 and 2 change when a long-lived mc process leaves and what starts its successor, never how the merger measures or lands a pull request, and never how the runner picks a step.
Step 3 changes when the merger writes `merges.json` and starts a mend, not what it answers or how a round runs.
done means every step done and every success criterion met (Martin, 2026-10-18); the 2026-08-29 'archived when done' ruling stands on that meaning.
A re-planned slot keeps its status; a blocked step is not released when it is retitled (Martin, 2026-10-03). `mc step ready` stays the way back.
The register stays the one place a step's state lives (ruling 21); no step writes plan state into PLAN.json except `met` in the last step.
Every existing `mc run`, `mc merge`, `mc step` and `mc repo watch` behaviour not named in a step stays as it is.
out_of_scope: A stable step id in the plan schema. Step 5 makes the title key survive renumbering; an id is a separate question.
Releasing a blocked step when a re-plan retitles it (ruled against 2026-10-03).
Changing how the merger measures or lands a pull request: the gate round, batching, restacking and mending are untouched.
The MERGES renderer (`mergesLines`, `src/mc/page-render.js`): it reads `merges.json` already, and step 3 only makes that file current.
The foreground page (`mc` at a terminal, `page-live.js`): a person's own process, restarted by that person.

The deployer (`deploy-run.js`, one process per deploy, bounded), the login agent (launchd runs `mc run start --if-was-running` once at login), `caffeinate` (not mc code) and `mc gate`'s detached `sh -c <test command>` (not mc code). None of these is a long-lived mc loop.
Step and mend sessions: they are model sessions, and the mc code around them is the runner (step) or the merger (mend), which steps 1 and 2 cover.
`mc run --update` fast-forwarding mc's checkout when no runner is running: it still says `mc run start`, and the processes move once the checkout does.
A reader for `runner/log/register.log` (`mc step --history`): grep reads it.
Renaming the 57 numbered step titles on memoro's main, or repairing the photo-analysis and photo-viewer register entries.
The by-index fallback `reconcileEntry` keeps for a plan whose keys are not unique.
Who typed `mc step ready log-page 1` on 2026-10-12, beyond what mc.log records (`cwd ~/memoro`, holder `martinforsberg@MacBookAir`).

success_criteria.criterion: A merger whose checkout HEAD differs from the commit it started on takes no new batch, finishes the round in flight, leaves the queue as it is, exits 0, and starts its successor when jobs remain; `mc merge watch` says `merger on <commit> · main <commit>` while they differ.
success_criteria.check: `node --test --import ./tests/_isolate-home.mjs tests/mc/merger.test.js tests/mc/merge-watch.test.js` passes, including 'a merger whose checkout moved takes no new batch, finishes the round in flight and leaves', 'succeed starts a merger only while jobs remain' and 'a merger behind its checkout is named on the line'.

success_criteria.criterion: The runner writes UPDATE itself when origin/main of mc's checkout has moved past its commit and the checkout can fast-forward; the repo watcher leaves after a refresh and starts its successor when its checkout moved; `mc run --update` prints one line per long-lived process; the page's MC line names any process behind its checkout.
success_criteria.check: `node --test --import ./tests/_isolate-home.mjs tests/mc/run.test.js tests/mc/run-control.test.js tests/mc/repo-watch.test.js tests/mc/page.test.js` passes, including the tests named in step 2.

success_criteria.criterion: While a batch's round runs, a member answered before it (closed, already merged, a restack refused) is already `red`, gone or `mending` in `merges.json`, and a mending member's mend has started.
success_criteria.check: `node --test --import ./tests/_isolate-home.mjs tests/mc/merger.test.js` passes, including the three tests named in step 3.

success_criteria.criterion: A plan whose steps are all done and whose criteria are not all met reads `unmet` with the criterion numbers, is neither archived nor closed, and is said once by the runner; `mc merge` and `mc merge --docs` refuse the last step's pull request while it leaves a criterion `met: false`.
success_criteria.check: `node --test --import ./tests/_isolate-home.mjs tests/mc/plan-schema.test.js tests/mc/merge-boundary.test.js tests/mc/merge-command.test.js tests/mc/docs-merge.test.js tests/mc/run.test.js` passes, including the tests named in step 4.

success_criteria.criterion: `stepKey` drops a leading ordinal, so a renumbered step keeps its state and the steps inserted before it start fresh; a slot carried by position keeps its status and loses the replaced step's pull request fields, with a comment saying so.
success_criteria.check: `node --test --import ./tests/_isolate-home.mjs tests/mc/register.test.js` passes, including the photo-viewer renumbering test named in step 5.

success_criteria.criterion: Every register write appends one JSON line to `~/mc/runner/log/register.log` naming the process (pid, ppid, parent, run id, argv shape, cwd, MC_STEP), and a log that cannot be written never fails the write.
success_criteria.check: `node --test --import ./tests/_isolate-home.mjs tests/mc/register.test.js` passes, including the tests named in step 6.

steps.title: The merger leaves for new code between rounds and starts its successor
steps.done_when: `serve` in `src/mc/merger.js` reads the checkout's HEAD before it takes each batch and, when it differs from `version.commit`, says so once, takes nothing new, lets the lanes in flight finish and returns 0 with the queue untouched; `merger-run.js` then calls the new `succeed`, which starts a merger only while jobs remain; `mc merge watch` names a merger behind its checkout; the new tests in `tests/mc/merger.test.js` and `tests/mc/merge-watch.test.js` pass; `mc gate` is green.
instruction: Why: on 2026-10-18 merger pid 95259 (`src/mc/merger-run.js`) started at 08:56Z on commit 3b51ff90 and served for 5 h 22 min on that code. Seven mc pull requests landed on main meanwhile, among them #948 (reuse a green `mc gate`, run only the delta), #949, #950 and #951; the merger itself landed #953 and #954. Martin found `mc merge` unusably slow and asked why the new code was not in place. The reason: `merger-run.js` reads its checkout and `commit` once (lines 42–46), and `serve` (`src/mc/merger.js` line 620) returns only when neither lane has anything to take (lines 741–755), which a busy queue never reaches. It took a SIGTERM at 14:18:36Z to end it. Martin's rule (2026-10-18): "Om man kör mc run --update så ska även merge och samtliga andra processer uppdateras automatiskt vid nästa möjlighet." This step makes the merger notice new code by itself; step 2 does the same for the runner and the repo watcher and adds `--update`'s lines.

What moves the checkout: the merger runs the installed mc's `merger-run.js` (`startMerger`, `installedMergerRun`, `src/mc/merger.js` lines 80 and 160–186), whose checkout is `~/memoro-cli`; the runner's handover fast-forwards that checkout (`handOver` → `fastForward`, `src/mc/run-control.js` lines 799 and 838), and step 2 makes the runner hand over by itself when main moves. So the merger only has to compare its checkout's HEAD with the commit it started on, with no network.

What starts the successor today: the runner's `sweepLanding` (`src/mc/run.js` around line 880, run inside `queue()` every pass, line ~2870) starts a merger when `merges.json` has a job that may go and no merger is alive, and `queueMerge` starts one on every `mc merge`. Both are kept as the fallback. The exiting merger also starts its successor itself, through `startMerger`, the same call `mc merge` makes, so a queue with jobs never waits for the runner's next pass. `startMerger` refuses while `merger.json` names a live pid, so it is called only after `serve` has released the file (its `finally`, line 807); two starters racing are settled by `takeMerger`'s `O_EXCL` (line 124), and the loser says 'another merger is running — leaving'.

In `serve` (`src/mc/merger.js` line 620) add two options after `appendRun = null`: `head = null` — `async () => <short sha> | null`, the checkout's HEAD now — and `onMoved = null` — `(from, to) => {}`, told once when the merger decides to leave for new code. Add `let movedTo = null;` beside `toldStop`. Add `async function codeMoved() { if (movedTo) return true; if (!head || !version?.commit || version.commit === 'unknown') return false; let now = null; try { now = await head(); } catch { now = null; } if (!now || sameCommit(now, version.commit)) return false; movedTo = now; say(`code moved ${version.commit} → ${now} — leaving after the rounds in flight; the next start serves on the new code`); try { onMoved?.(version.commit, now); } catch { /* a line, not the merger */ } return true; }` and a module-level `function sameCommit(a, b) { const x = String(a || ''); const y = String(b || ''); return Boolean(x && y) && (x.startsWith(y) || y.startsWith(x)); }` with the comment 'two short shas of different lengths name one commit when one starts the other' (the rule `requestUpdate` uses, `src/mc/run-control.js` line 754).

In `loop` (line 702), right after the `stopping()` block (lines 705–710) and before the `lock(root, …)` that takes a batch (line 711), add: `if (await codeMoved()) { leaving = true; changed(); return; }`. A lane whose round is in flight is not interrupted: it reaches the top of its loop when its round is answered and returns at `if (leaving) return;` (line 704). The queue is not touched: jobs stay `queued`, and nothing is marked `landing`. An idle lane waits at most `MERGER_POLL_MS` (15 s, line 85) before it looks again (line 737), so an idle merger leaves within 15 s of the checkout moving. After `await Promise.all(lanes.map(loop));` (line 797) the mends block becomes `if (mends) { if (toldStop || movedTo) mends.stop(); await mends.idle(); }`: a mend not started yet is dropped (its entry stays `mending`, and the successor puts it back in line, lines 650–657) and a running one is waited for, exactly as on a stop. In the `finally`, after `if (toldStop) say('left');`, add `if (movedTo && !toldStop) say(`left for ${movedTo}`);`. `serve` still returns 0. Update the doc comment above `serve` (lines 611–619) with one sentence: before each batch it asks `head()`, and a checkout that has moved past `version.commit` ends it like a stop, between rounds, with the queue left as it is.

Add to `src/mc/merger.js`, after `startMerger`: `/** After a merger left for new code: a successor on the installed checkout while jobs remain in line, or nothing. Returns the line it said. */ export function succeed({ root, movedTo = null, read = realRead, start = startMerger, say = () => {} } = {}) { const waiting = inLine(parseQueue(read(mergesPath(root)))).length; if (!waiting) { const line = 'nothing in line — no successor started; the next mc merge starts one'; say(line); return line; } const next = start({ root }); const line = next.pid ? `successor pid ${next.pid} started on ${movedTo || 'the new code'} for ${waiting} job${waiting === 1 ? '' : 's'} in line` : `no successor started (${next.error || 'no pid'}) — the runner\'s next pass starts one`; say(line); return line; }`. Import `inLine` from `./merge-queue.js` beside `parseQueue` if it is not imported yet. Also add `export function installedHead({ env = process.env, git = (cwd, args) => spawnSync('git', ['-C', cwd, ...args], { encoding: 'utf8', timeout: 5000 }) } = {}) { const install = sourceLinkedInstallations(env).find((item) => item.command === 'mc'); if (!install) return null; const r = git(install.root, ['rev-parse', '--short', 'HEAD']); return r?.status === 0 ? String(r.stdout || '').trim() || null : null; }` with the doc comment 'the HEAD of the checkout `mc` on PATH runs from: what the next merger would run. Local, no network.' (`sourceLinkedInstallations` is already imported, line 57; add `spawnSync` to the `node:child_process` import).

In `src/mc/merger-run.js`: replace the one-shot commit read (lines 45–46) with `const headNow = async () => { const r = await runTool('git', ['-C', checkout, 'rev-parse', '--short', 'HEAD'], { timeoutMs: 5000 }); return r.status === 0 ? String(r.stdout).trim() || null : null; };` and `const commit = (await headNow()) || 'unknown';`. Pass `head: headNow` and `onMoved: (from, to) => { movedTo = to; }` to `serve` (declare `let movedTo = null;` above). After `serve` returns and before `process.exit(code)`: `if (movedTo && !stopping) succeed({ root, movedTo, say });` (import `succeed` from `./merger.js`). A merger asked to stop by SIGTERM starts no successor: a stop means stop. Rewrite the header comment's second paragraph: SIGTERM and SIGINT let the jobs in flight finish and then leave; a checkout that moves past the commit it started on does the same between rounds and starts a successor on the new code while jobs remain.

`mc merge watch`, in `src/mc/merge-watch.js`: `watchState(entries, { repo, pr, merger = null, ordered = () => true, head = null } = {})` (line 46) sets `state.code = `merger on ${merger.commit} · main ${head}`` when `merger?.commit && head` and the two are not the same commit (use the same prefix rule; add a local `sameCommit`). `lineOf` (line 73) appends ` — ${state.code}` to the queued, waiting and landing lines when `state.code` is set. `watchLine` (line 98) also prints when `(prev.code || null) !== (next.code || null)`. `watch` takes `readHead = () => null` and passes `head: readHead()` to `watchState` each poll (line 138). `followMerge` (line 186) passes `readHead: deps.readHead || (() => installedHead())` (import `installedHead` from `./merger.js`). The commit is the one `merger.json` keeps (`takeMerger` writes it, `readMerger` returns it).

Tests in `tests/mc/merger.test.js`, inside `describe('serve — the loop')` (line 292), with its `take`, `release`, `ONE_LANE`, `JOB`, `lock`, `queue()` and `green`. (1) 'a merger whose checkout moved takes no new batch, finishes the round in flight and leaves': queue `[{ ...JOB, pr: 1, since: 'a', step: null }, { ...JOB, pr: 2, since: 'b', step: null }]`; `const heads = ['aaa1111', 'bbb2222']; const said = []; const moved = [];` `serve({ root, lock, take, release, ...ONE_LANE, say: (l) => said.push(l), version: { checkout: '~/memoro-cli', commit: 'aaa1111' }, head: async () => heads.shift() ?? 'bbb2222', onMoved: (a, b) => moved.push([a, b]), land: async ([job]) => { landed.push(job.pr); return green; } })` returns 0; `landed` deepEquals `[1]`; `queue().map((e) => [e.pr, e.state])` deepEquals `[[2, 'queued']]`; `said` includes 'code moved aaa1111 → bbb2222 — leaving after the rounds in flight; the next start serves on the new code' and 'left for bbb2222'; `moved` deepEquals `[['aaa1111', 'bbb2222']]`. (2) 'a head that reads the same commit, a longer sha of it, or nothing changes nothing': three runs over the same two-job queue with `head` returning `'aaa1111'`, `'aaa1111ff'` and `null`; each lands `[1, 2]` and says no 'code moved' line. (3) 'without a version or a head the loop is as before': every existing serve test passes unchanged — they pass neither. (4) 'a mend not yet started when the code moves is dropped and its entry stays mending': model it on 'while a mend is pending, the same lane takes and answers its next job' (line 1094) with `mendAtOnce: 1`: two reds that both mend, the first mend held open, `head` moving after the first batch; when `serve` resolves, the second job's entry is `mending` and its mend never ran.

Tests for `succeed`, in a new `describe('succeed — a successor after new code')` in the same file: 'succeed starts a merger only while jobs remain': with `merges.json` holding one `queued` entry and `start: () => ({ pid: 4321, started: true })`, the returned line is 'successor pid 4321 started on bbb2222 for 1 job in line'; with an empty queue `start` is never called and the line is 'nothing in line — no successor started; the next mc merge starts one'; with `start: () => ({ pid: null, error: 'spawn failed' })` the line is 'no successor started (spawn failed) — the runner\'s next pass starts one'. A queue holding only a `red` entry counts as nothing in line (`inLine`).

Tests in `tests/mc/merge-watch.test.js`, inside `describe('watchState and watchLine')` (line 158): 'a merger behind its checkout is named on the line': `watchState([{ repo: 'memoro', pr: 7, state: 'queued', since: 'a' }], { repo: 'memoro', pr: 7, merger: { pid: 1, commit: 'aaa1111' }, head: 'bbb2222' })` gives `code` 'merger on aaa1111 · main bbb2222', and `watchLine(null, state, { pr: 7 })` ends with ' — merger on aaa1111 · main bbb2222'; with `head: 'aaa1111'` there is no `code`; and `watchLine(stateWithout, stateWith)` is not null.

Docs: in `docs/technical/mc-merge.md`, after the paragraph on the mend (around line 946–969), add one paragraph: on 2026-10-18 a merger served 5 h 22 min on 3b51ff90 while seven mc pull requests landed, because it read its commit once and left only on an empty queue. Since then it reads its checkout's HEAD before each batch; a HEAD past the commit it started on ends it between rounds, like a stop, with the queue untouched, and it starts its successor through `startMerger` while jobs remain (`succeed`). The runner's `sweepLanding` and the next `mc merge` still start one when none lives. `mc merge watch` adds `merger on <commit> · main <commit>` while the two differ. Changelog: add `changelog.d/merger-leaves-for-new-code.md` with `section: Fixed` and one entry saying the same in two sentences.
`mc gate tests/mc/merger.test.js tests/mc/merge-watch.test.js`, then `mc gate`, `mc publish`, `mc merge memoro-cli <pr>`.

steps.title: mc run --update reaches every long-lived process, the runner and the repo watcher follow new code by themselves, and the page names a process behind its checkout
steps.done_when: The runner writes UPDATE itself in `chores` when origin/main of mc's checkout has moved past its commit and the checkout is clean and can fast-forward; `repo-watch-run.js` leaves after a refresh when its checkout's HEAD moved and starts its successor; `requestUpdate` in `src/mc/run-control.js` adds one line per long-lived process; the page's MC line names any process whose commit differs from the checkout's; the new tests in `tests/mc/run.test.js`, `tests/mc/run-control.test.js`, `tests/mc/repo-watch.test.js` and `tests/mc/page.test.js` pass; `mc gate` is green.
instruction: Why: Martin, 2026-10-18: "Om man kör mc run --update så ska även merge och samtliga andra processer uppdateras automatiskt vid nästa möjlighet." Step 1 made the merger leave when its checkout moves. This step makes landing a pull request enough: the runner notices main moved and hands over (which fast-forwards the checkout), the merger and the watcher see the checkout move and follow, and `--update` only makes it immediate and says what each process will do.

The long-lived mc processes on origin/main, measured with `grep -rn 'detached: true' src` and `ps` on 2026-10-18: (a) the runner, `mc run` (`src/mc/run.js` `runLoop`), which already hands over on UPDATE (`handOver`, `src/mc/run-control.js` line 799) but never notices new code by itself; (b) the merger, `src/mc/merger-run.js`, done in step 1; (c) the repo watcher, `src/mc/repo-watch-run.js`, started by `mc repo watch start` (`startWatcher`, `src/mc/repo-watch.js` line 73), a loop of refreshes (`watchLoop`, `src/mc/repo-watch-loop.js` line 41) whose SIGTERM handler already means 'finish the round, then leave'. Not long-lived mc loops, and left alone: the deployer (`deploy-run.js`, one per deploy), the login agent (launchd runs `mc run start --if-was-running` once), `caffeinate` (`stay-awake.js`), `mc gate`'s detached `sh -c` test command, `mc shot`'s viewer, the dev servers (`test-environment.js`, memoro code), and step and mend sessions, which are model sessions inside the runner and the merger.

The runner, in `src/mc/run.js`. Add `const codeNoticed = new Set();` beside `stopSeen` (around line 913) and a function `noticeNewCode()` in `createRunner` near `markRunner` (line ~3205): `const dir = mcCheckout({ exists: deps.exists }); if (!dir || !marked?.commit || updateRequested()) return; const main = gitOut(dir, ['rev-parse', '--short', 'origin/main']); if (!main || sameCommit(main, marked.commit) || codeNoticed.has(main)) return; codeNoticed.add(main); const dirty = gitOut(dir, ['status', '--porcelain']); const ff = deps.git(dir, ['merge-base', '--is-ancestor', 'HEAD', 'origin/main']).ok; if (dirty || !ff) { say(`update: origin/main is ${main} and this runner is on ${marked.commit}, but ${dir} ${dirty ? 'has uncommitted changes' : 'has diverged from origin/main'} — not handing over; mc run --update once it is clean`); return; } deps.write(paths.update, `${stamp()}\n`); say(`update: origin/main is ${main} and this runner is on ${marked.commit} — UPDATE written by the runner; it hands over at its next look`);`. `gitOut` (line 690) returns trimmed stdout or null, so a clean tree is `''` and falsy. Call `noticeNewCode()` in `chores()` (around line 3133) right after `const { plans } = queue();`: `queue()` has just fetched `~/memoro-cli` (it fetches every repository, line ~2864), which is the checkout `mcCheckout` names, so this costs no network. `codeNoticed` keeps one line per origin/main sha per process, so a dirty checkout is said once, not every pass. Add `sameCommit` (the prefix rule of `requestUpdate`, `src/mc/run-control.js` line 754) as a small local function if run.js has none. The handover that follows is the existing one (ruling 28): the old runner finishes its steps in flight and takes nothing new, and the successor starts at once on the fast-forwarded checkout.

The watcher. In `src/mc/repo-watch.js`: add `export function checkoutHead({ dir = fileURLToPath(new URL('../..', import.meta.url)).replace(/\/$/u, ''), run = execFileSync } = {}) { try { return String(run('git', ['-C', dir, 'rev-parse', '--short', 'HEAD'], { encoding: 'utf8', timeout: 5000 })).trim() || null; } catch { return null; } }`. `startWatcher` writes `commit: checkoutHead()` into the pid file record (line ~100) beside `runner`. `watcherState` returns `commit: running ? record?.commit || null : null`. In `src/mc/repo-watch-loop.js`, `watchLoop` takes `afterRound = null` and, after the round's log line and before `if (shouldStop()) break;` (line 52), runs `if (afterRound) { try { if (await afterRound()) break; } catch { /* a check, not the loop */ } }`. In `src/mc/repo-watch-run.js`: `const started = checkoutHead();` before the loop; `let movedTo = null;` `const afterRound = () => { const now = checkoutHead(); if (!started || !now || sameCommit(now, started)) return false; movedTo = now; return true; };` and pass `afterRound` to `watchLoop`. Move the pid-file removal (lines 47–53) into a function `release()` and call it after the loop. Then, when `movedTo` is set and `stopping` is not: `log(`code moved ${started} → ${movedTo} — left after this refresh; the next start watches on the new code`)`, `const next = startWatcher({ intervalMs }); log(next.ok ? `successor pid ${next.pid}` : `no successor started (${next.reason})`);`. The release must come first: `startWatcher` refuses while the pid file names a live watcher, and this process is still alive. The successor runs `RUNNER`, the same path in the same checkout, which now holds the new code. The header comment gains one sentence saying this.

`mc run --update`, in `src/mc/run-control.js`. Add `export function processLines({ root, head = null, readMergerFn = readMerger, watcher = watcherState, read = (path) => { try { return readFileSync(path, 'utf8'); } catch { return null; } } } = {})` returning an array of lines, one per process: the merger from `readMergerFn({ root })` and the watcher from `watcher()`. Merger alive: `const landing = parseQueue(read(mergesPath(root))).filter((e) => e.state === 'landing').map((e) => `#${e.pr}`);` then, when `head` and its `commit` differ, `merger: pid ${m.pid} on ${m.commit}, checkout at ${head} — leaves after ${landing.length ? `the round of ${landing.join(' ')}` : 'its next look'} and starts its successor on ${head}`, else `merger: pid ${m.pid} on ${m.commit} — leaves after ${…same…} once the checkout moves, and starts its successor on the new code`. No merger: `merger: none running — the next one starts on the checkout's code`. Watcher running: `repo watch: pid ${w.pid} on ${w.commit || '?'} — leaves after its refresh in flight once the checkout moves, and starts its successor`; not running: `repo watch: not running`. Import `readMerger` from `./merger.js`, `watcherState` from `./repo-watch.js`, and `parseQueue`, `mergesPath` from `./merge-queue.js`; keep the imports top-level only if run-control.js already imports from those modules eagerly, else import them inside `requestUpdate` with `await import` and make `requestUpdate` async (its caller `src/mc/commands/run.js` line 109 already returns its result; await it there). In `requestUpdate` (line 716), append `...processLines({ root: <the work root>, head: dir ? head(dir, deps) : null, … })` to `lines` on every return that hands over or is already draining (lines 731, 746 and 773) and on the 'nothing to update' return (line 756), because a merger can be behind its checkout while the runner is current. Tests inject `readMergerFn` and `watcher` through `deps` (`deps.readMerger`, `deps.watcherState`), so `realControlDeps` gains `readMerger: (options) => readMerger(options)` and `watcherState: () => watcherState()`. Update the doc comment above `requestUpdate` and `usage()` in `src/mc/commands/run.js` (line 66): `--update` moves the runner now, and the merger and the repo watcher at their next safe point, each starting a successor on the new code.

The page's MC line. In `src/mc/page-collect.js`, `mcSection` (line 978) takes `processes = []` (`[{ name, pid, commit }]`) and returns `behind_checkout: head ? processes.filter((p) => p?.commit && !sameCommit(p.commit, head)) : []` (`sameCommit` exists at line 144). The `collectPage` call (around line 1618) passes `processes: [readMerger({ root }) && { name: 'merger', ...readMerger({ root }) }, (() => { const w = watcherState({ root: home }); return w.running ? { name: 'repo watch', pid: w.pid, commit: w.commit } : null; })()].filter(Boolean)` — file reads and a `kill(pid, 0)`, no network, as the rest of the page. In `src/mc/page-render.js` `mcLine` (around line 1405), add to `rest`, after the predecessor part, one part per item: `{ text: `${p.name} pid ${p.pid} on ${p.commit} · checkout ${info.head}`, styles: ['yellow'] }`. Update `mcLine`'s doc comment with one sentence.

steps.title: The merger writes an answer given before the round to merges.json at once, and a mend starts when the mend line frees
steps.done_when: `landJob` in `src/mc/merger.js` calls a new `onAnswer` after each `tell`, outside any lock; `serve` writes that one job's entry (`dequeue`, `markMending` or `markRed`) and starts its mend at once, and its post-round loop skips jobs already written; the three new tests in `tests/mc/merger.test.js` pass; `mc gate` is green.
instruction: Why: on 2026-10-10 merger 88564 took the batch #13375 #13397 #13400 #13405. Before the round, `landJob` answered #13400 'closed on GitHub' and set #13397 aside for a mend (restack conflict); the round went on with #13375 #13405 for 9 minutes. For all of it the page drew four as landing ('same round as #13375') and #13397 not as mending, and `merges.json` said `landing` for all four. #13397's mend started at 22:17:12, when the round ended, although the mend before it had ended at 22:15:32. Cause, on origin/main: `landJob` (`src/mc/merger.js` line 405) answers before the round in two places, a restack refusal (line 437) and GitHub's MERGED or CLOSED (lines 445–451), through its local `answer()` (lines 423–429). `answer()` calls `tell`, which writes the register at once (lines 566–590), and nothing writes `merges.json`. `serve` writes the queue only after `land()` returns (the answers loop, lines 777–790) and starts the mends there (line 791). The page (`mergesSection`, `src/mc/page-collect.js` line 594) and `mc merge watch` read `merges.json`, so fixing the writer fixes both.

The lock trap: `tell` → `updateStep` takes `realLock` (`src/mc/register.js` line 439), and `merges.json` is guarded by the same lock (every `lock(root, …)` in `serve`). The lock is not re-entrant: taken again by the same process it waits `LOCK_WAIT_MS` (5 s) and then writes anyway. So `onAnswer` is called after `tell` has returned, never from inside a `lock` callback, and `serve`'s writer takes the lock itself.

In `landJob` add the option `onAnswer = null` (after `mayMend`, with the comment 'told each answer as it is given, after the register is written: `serve` writes the queue and starts a mend from it'). At the end of `answer()`, after `await tell(…)`: `if (onAnswer) { try { await onAnswer({ job, landed, report, ...(mending ? { mending: true } : {}) }); } catch (error) { say(`${job.repo} #${job.pr}: the queue could not be told (${error?.message || error}) — written after the round`); } }`. `landerFor` (line 544) becomes `(batch, lane, extra = {}) => landJob(batch, { ...deps, lane, ...extra })`.

In `serve`: add `const written = new Set();` and `const keyOf = (job) => `${job.repo}#${job.pr}`;` beside `inFlight`. Add `const writeAnswer = async ({ job, landed, report, mending }) => { const at = now().toISOString(); const reason = `${report?.stopped_at || 'unknown'}: ${report?.reason || 'the round said nothing'}`; lock(root, () => { let entries = parseQueue(read(mergesPath(root))); entries = landed && report?.ok && report.merged ? dequeue(entries, job) : mending && mends ? markMending(entries, job, { reason, stopped_at: report?.stopped_at || null, started: at }) : markRed(entries, job, { reason, answered: at }); write(mergesPath(root), entries); }); written.add(keyOf(job)); if (mending && mends) mends.start(job, report).then(changed); changed(); };`. The merged test is the same expression the post-round loop uses (`report?.ok && report.merged`, line 783), so an already-merged answer (`alreadyMerged`, `ok: true, merged: true`) is dequeued. The call at line 764 becomes `await land(batch, lane, { onAnswer: writeAnswer })`. In the post-round block (lines 777–791), filter first: `const left = answers.filter((one) => !written.has(keyOf(one.job)));`, and use `left` for both `toMend` and the loop; skip the `lock`/`write` when `left` is empty. After the block, `for (const one of batch) written.delete(keyOf(one));` so a job queued again later is written again. The round's own answers (line 516) also pass through `answer()` and so through `onAnswer`; the filtered loop then covers only the `threw` path (line 768) and a `land` that ignores its third argument, as the tests' stubs do.

Since step 1, `serve` also takes `head` and `onMoved`; keep both, and keep the `codeMoved()` check where step 1 put it. A mend started mid-round runs beside the round, as mends already do (`mendLine`, `src/mc/mend.js` line 306, `MEND_AT_ONCE` 1, line 46); `mendLine` starts it when its slot frees.

Update the doc comment above `landJob` (lines 399–404): each answer is written to the register and told to `onAnswer` when it is given, so the queue and the page know a pre-round answer for the whole round. And the comment above the post-round block: what is left there is what `onAnswer` did not write.

Tests in `tests/mc/merger.test.js`, inside `describe('already merged or closed on GitHub (merger-hardening step 2)')` (line 530), with its `MEMORO`, `jobFor`, `registerBatch`, `stubGh`, `OPEN`, `MERGED`, `CLOSED` and `two`. For each, write the three jobs to `mergesPath(root)` and run `serve({ root, lock, take: () => true, release: () => {}, ...ONE_LANE, gh, say: m.deps.say, now: m.deps.now, land: (batch, lane, extra) => landJob(batch, { ...m.deps, ...extra, mergeRound: async (options) => { seen = queue().map((e) => [e.pr, e.state]); return m.deps.mergeRound(options); } }) })`. (1) 'a member closed on GitHub is red in merges.json while the others\' round runs': states `{ 11: OPEN, 12: CLOSED, 13: OPEN }`; `seen` deepEquals `[[11, 'landing'], [12, 'red'], [13, 'landing']]`, and #12's entry in `seen`-time queue has reason 'closed: #12 was closed on GitHub without merging'. (2) 'a member already merged is gone from merges.json while the round runs': `{ 11: OPEN, 12: MERGED, 13: OPEN }`; `seen` deepEquals `[[11, 'landing'], [13, 'landing']]`. (3) 'a restack refusal that gets its mend is mending, and its mend has started, before the round ends': no GitHub states needed beyond OPEN for all three; `#12` carries `parent: { project: null, index: null, pr: 5, sha: 'abc' }` and a `branch: 'mb-12'`; pass `moveOntoMain: (job) => (job.pr === 12 ? { ok: false, reason: 'moving #12 onto main after #5 landed conflicts in a.js' } : { ok: true, moved: true })` and `mayMend: (job) => job.pr === 12` in the deps given to `landJob`, and to `serve` `mend: async (job) => { mendStarted.push([job.pr, roundDone]); return { outcome: 'nothing', line: 'gave up', status: 0, seconds: 0 }; }` with `let roundDone = false;` set true in a wrapped `mergeRound` after it returns. Assert `mendStarted` deepEquals `[[12, false]]` and `seen` has `[12, 'mending']`. Every existing test in the file passes unchanged.

Docs: in `docs/technical/mc-merge.md`, the paragraph 'Already merged on GitHub' (line 927): add that a job answered before the round — merged, closed, or a restack refused — is written to `merges.json` the moment it is answered, so the page and `mc merge watch` never draw it as landing, and a restack red that gets its mend starts it as soon as the mend line is free (2026-10-10, #13397 waited 100 s for the round to end). Changelog: `changelog.d/merger-answers-at-once.md`, `section: Fixed`.
`mc gate tests/mc/merger.test.js`, then `mc gate`, `mc publish`, `mc merge memoro-cli <pr>`.

steps.title: A plan is done only when its criteria are met: an unmet state, and a door for the last step
steps.done_when: `planState` in `src/mc/plan-schema.js` returns `unmet` with the 1-based criterion numbers when every step is done and a criterion is not `met: true`; `deliverableStep` and `planSummary` say why; the page and `mc status` show it; the runner says it once; nothing archives or closes it; the new `criteriaDoor` in `src/mc/merge-boundary.js` refuses the plan's last step's pull request in `mc merge`, `mc merge --docs` and the runner's own queueing while it leaves a criterion unmet; the new tests pass; `mc gate` is green.
instruction: Why: on 2026-10-11 memoro `photo-analysis` step 5, the close, was blocked: criteria 0–2 needed production checks Martin runs himself. A foreign PR (#13549) was booked as that step (fixed by #894), the register said done, and #13577 archived the project with criteria 0–2 still `met: false` on main. The archive triggers on `plan.status === 'done'` alone (`donePlans`, `src/mc/archive-plan.js` line 38, called from `archiveDone`, `src/mc/run.js` line 1384), and a plan's status is derived from its steps alone (`planState`, `src/mc/plan-schema.js` line 408). Martin, 2026-10-18: "success criteria and done belong together." So the fix is where the state is derived, not a guard on the archive.

The state. In `planState` (line 408), in the `index === -1` branch where no step is landing (line 415), before `return { status: 'done', … }`: `const unmet = (Array.isArray(plan?.success_criteria) ? plan.success_criteria : []).map((c, i) => (c?.met === true ? null : i + 1)).filter(Boolean); if (unmet.length) return { status: 'unmet', index: -1, step: null, unmet };`. Extend the doc comment: a plan whose steps are all done is done only when every criterion is met (Martin, 2026-10-18); otherwise it is `unmet`, with the criteria's numbers. Add `export function unmetWords(unmet)` returning `success criterion 2 is not met on main — measure it and set met: true in a pull request, or add a step that does` for one and `success criteria 2, 3 are not met on main — measure them and set met: true in a pull request, or add a step that does` for several. In `deliverableStep` (line 443), after the `done` line (448): `if (state.status === 'unmet') return { step: null, index: -1, reason: 'unmet', why: `every step is done, but ${unmetWords(state.unmet)}`, problems: [] };`. `planSummary` (line 384) then returns `status: 'unmet'` and that `next` with no change, because it takes `status` from `planState` and `next` from `why`.

What follows by itself, with no code change, and must be checked rather than assumed: `donePlans` (archive-plan.js line 38), `closable` (`src/mc/close-workarea.js` line 71, says 'the plan is unmet'), `closeWorkareas` (run.js line 1762), `tidyQueue` (`src/mc/run-plan.js` line 146) and a `project` blocker's release (`src/mc/step-release.js` line 112) all test `=== 'done'`, so an unmet plan is not archived, its workarea is not closed, and a step waiting on it keeps waiting. `chooseKind` (run-plan.js line 357) answers `skip:unmet`. The page draws the project row's `status` and `next` (`src/mc/page-collect.js` around line 1194) and counts statuses (`statusesOf`, line 1061); add `unmet: ['yellow', 'bold']` to `STATUS_TONE` (`src/mc/page-render.js` line 62) with the comment 'steps all done, a criterion not met: somebody has to measure'. `unmet` is five columns, inside the status cell. `mc status` prints `planSummary`'s status and next (`src/mc/status-project.js` lines 58 and 141).

The runner says it once. In `createRunner` add `const saidUnmet = new Set();` and in `chores()` after `const { plans } = queue();` (around line 3140, after step 2's `noticeNewCode()`): `for (const record of plans) { if (record?.status !== 'unmet' || saidUnmet.has(record.project)) continue; saidUnmet.add(record.project); say(`${record.project}: ${record.next} — not archived`); }`.

The door. `mc merge` compares a step's PLAN.json at the door already (`planBoundary`, `src/mc/merge-boundary.js` line 80, called from `src/mc/commands/repo.js` line 418 with the register's step index, and from the runner's `landForSession`, `src/mc/run.js` line 2802). It is the right place, with three facts that shape it: `planBoundary` returns early when the head plan is byte-identical to the base (line 111), which is exactly the case of a last step that did not touch `met`; a docs-only pull request, the usual close-out, never reaches it, because `mc merge` routes it to `runDocsMerge` (`src/mc/commands/merge.js` lines 48–53) with no boundary at all; and a plan with no criteria cannot occur, because the schema refuses one (`validateCriteria`, plan-schema.js line 220). So the check is its own function, called from all three doors, and it fails open like `planBoundary` on anything it cannot read.

Add to `src/mc/merge-boundary.js`: `export async function criteriaDoor({ repoPath, pr, git, gh, step = undefined, env = process.env, entries = [] } = {})`. Ask `gh pr view <pr> --json headRefName,baseRefName` as `planBoundary` does (lines 84–90); `git fetch origin --prune`; find the project's `PLAN.json` path from `ls-tree -r --name-only origin/<base> -- docs/project` with `projectForBranch` (lines 95–105). `const target = step !== undefined ? step : stepForMerge({ env, head, entries });` (import `stepForMerge` from `./merge-step.js`); no target → `notChecked`. Read `git show origin/<head>:<path>` and `readPlanText`; no plan → `notChecked`. When `target.index !== plan.steps.length - 1` → `{ checked: true, ok: true, problems: [] }`. Else compute `unmet` as in `planState`; empty → ok; otherwise `{ checked: true, ok: false, unmet, problems: [`step ${target.index + 1} is the plan\'s last, and ${unmetWords(unmet)} in this pull request — or mc step failed --reason "…" naming what could not be measured`] }` (import `unmetWords` from `./plan-schema.js`). Any `status !== 0` or parse failure on the way → `notChecked`. Doc comment: the last step is where a plan becomes done, and done means its criteria met (Martin, 2026-10-18), so its pull request does not land while it leaves one `met: false`; the session measures, or fails visibly.

Wire it. (1) `src/mc/commands/repo.js`, after the plan-trespass block (ends ~line 433): `if (step) { const door = await (deps.criteriaDoor || criteriaDoor)({ repoPath, pr: opts.pr, git: deps.git, gh: deps.gh, step: { project: step.project, index: step.index } }); if (door.checked && !door.ok) { … }` recording the round exactly like the trespass block but with `stopped_at: 'unmet-criteria'`, writing `mc: unmet-criteria — ${problem}` per problem and returning 1. (2) `src/mc/commands/merge.js`, right before `runDocsMerge` (line 53): `const root = deps.root || workRoot(deps.env || process.env); const io = { read: deps.read, write: deps.writeJson, lock: deps.lock }` (drop undefined keys as `bookDocsLanding` does), `const door = await (deps.criteriaDoor || criteriaDoor)({ repoPath, pr: opts.pr, gh: deps.gh, git: deps.git, env: deps.env || process.env, entries: listEntries(root, io) }); if (door.checked && !door.ok) { for (const p of door.problems) stderr.write(`mc: unmet-criteria — ${p}\n`); return 1; }`. A planning session's pull request is nobody's step, so `stepForMerge` returns null and it passes. (3) `landForSession` (`src/mc/run.js` line 2799), after the trespass block: `const door = deps.criteriaDoor ? await deps.criteriaDoor({ repoPath: worktree, pr: number, step: { project: name, index } }) : { checked: false };` and on a refusal the same `redPatch` path with `stopped_at: 'unmet-criteria'` and `reason: `unmet-criteria — ${door.problems.join('; ')}``. Add `criteriaDoor: (options) => criteriaDoor(options)` beside `planBoundary` in the runner's real deps (line 583).

The step role. In `canon/roles/step.md`, under step 3 of 'Otherwise, build it' (the `plan-trespass` bullet, line 38), add a bullet: `unmet-criteria` — you are the plan's last step and a success criterion is still `met: false` in your pull request: run its `check`, set `met: true` on each you measured, commit, push and `mc merge` again; one you cannot measure is `mc step failed --reason` naming it. And in the paragraph at line 13: `met` on criteria you actually met, and on the last step every criterion, or the PR does not land.

Tests in `tests/mc/plan-schema.test.js`: 'every step done with a criterion unmet is unmet, with its numbers': a valid plan with two `done` steps and criteria `[{ met: true, … }, { met: false, … }, { met: false, … }]`: `planState(plan)` deepEquals `{ status: 'unmet', index: -1, step: null, unmet: [2, 3] }`; `planSummary(plan).status` is `'unmet'` and `.next` is 'every step is done, but success criteria 2, 3 are not met on main — measure them and set met: true in a pull request, or add a step that does'; `deliverableStep(plan).reason` is `'unmet'`; with every criterion `met: true`, `planState(plan).status` is `'done'`; with one unmet, the singular sentence.

Tests in `tests/mc/merge-boundary.test.js`, with its `plan()` and `tools()`: 'criteriaDoor refuses the last step while a criterion is unmet': `criteriaDoor({ repoPath: '/x', pr: 671, git, gh, step: { project: 'step-lands-itself', index: 1 } })` → `checked` true, `ok` false, `unmet` `[1]`, `problems[0]` starts with 'step 2 is the plan\'s last, and success criterion 1 is not met on main'; the same with the head plan's criterion `met: true` → ok; `step: { …, index: 0 }` → ok; `step: null` → `checked` false; `gh` failing → `checked` false. In `tests/mc/merge-command.test.js`, `deps()` (line 52) gains `criteriaDoor: async () => door || { checked: false }` with a `door` option; a test 'the last step with an unmet criterion is refused at the door and nothing is queued' asserts exit 1, stderr contains 'mc: unmet-criteria — ', and no queue write (follow the trespass test at line ~172). In `tests/mc/docs-merge.test.js`, inside 'books the landing on the step whose pull request it is' (line 131): `landing()` takes `criteriaDoor` and passes it in the deps; 'a docs-only last step with an unmet criterion is refused before it lands' asserts `code` 1, `out` matches `/unmet-criteria — /u`, `step.status` still `'running'`, and the gh stub saw no `pr merge` call. In `tests/mc/run.test.js`, beside 'a plan trespass found at the runner\'s door is the step\'s red' (line 1650): the same with `f.deps.criteriaDoor = async () => ({ checked: true, ok: false, unmet: [1], problems: ['step 1 is the plan\'s last'] })` and `f.deps.planBoundary` passing: the step is `ready`, `attempts` 1, reason 'unmet-criteria — step 1 is the plan\'s last'.

Tests in `tests/mc/run.test.js` for the state: the file's `plan()` helper (line 457) writes `met: false`, which would turn every finished fixture `unmet`. Give it `met = status === 'done'` as a parameter and write `success_criteria: [{ met, criterion: 'It is done.', check: 'The row is in runs.tsv.' }]`, so `done()` (line 2951) stays a finished plan. Add 'a plan with every step done and a criterion unmet is not archived, and is said once': `fixture({ plans: { memoro: { over: plan({ status: 'done', met: false }) } }, projectLog: { memoro: LOG_HEAD }, session: okSession() })`, two `round(createRunner({ deps: f.deps }))`; `f.calls.rm` is empty, no `gh` call creates a pull request, and runner.log has exactly one line matching `/over: every step is done, but success criterion 1 is not met on main/u`. Then run `node --test --import ./tests/_isolate-home.mjs tests/mc/*.test.js tests/mc/commands/*.test.js`; where an existing test fails only because its fixture's finished plan has `met: false` (likely in `register.test.js`, `page.test.js`, `step-release.test.js`, `status-*.test.js`), set that fixture's criteria `met: true`; change no assertion. List the files you touched this way in the PR body.

Docs: `docs/project/README.md`, the paragraph 'The plan has **no status of its own**' (around line 116): a plan whose steps are all done is done when every success criterion is met, and `unmet` otherwise; the runner archives only a done plan. `docs/technical/mc-run.md` § step 4 *Archive* (line 276): every plan that is done — every step done and every criterion met; an `unmet` plan is said once and left. `docs/technical/mc-merge.md`: the door's `unmet-criteria` refusal, in `mc merge`, `mc merge --docs` and the runner's queueing. Changelog: `changelog.d/done-means-criteria-met.md`, `section: Changed`.

`mc gate tests/mc/plan-schema.test.js tests/mc/merge-boundary.test.js tests/mc/merge-command.test.js tests/mc/docs-merge.test.js tests/mc/run.test.js`, then `mc gate`, `mc publish`, `mc merge memoro-cli <pr>`.

steps.title: Step keys ignore a leading ordinal, and a slot carried by position loses the replaced step's pull request fields
steps.done_when: `stepKey` in `src/mc/register.js` drops a leading ordinal through a new exported `keyOf`; `reconcileEntry` compares stored keys through `keyOf`, and its positional fallback keeps the slot's status, clears `pr`, `branch`, `attempts`, `stacked_on`, `red` and `interrupted` (keeping `pr` on a done step), appends one comment, and returns `carried`; the new tests in `tests/mc/register.test.js` pass; `mc gate` is green.
instruction: Why: memoro #13580 (2026-10-12) put three steps before `photo-viewer`'s close and renamed it from '5. The close' to '8. The close'. The register gave the old close's entry to the new step 5, '5. The reserve shrinks…': `blocked` on `martin-phone-fling-check`, branch `photo-viewer-8`, `stacked_on` #13527, and the old close's comments, one of them telling the next session to 'mc merge memoro 13528', a closed PR. Cause, in `src/mc/register.js`: `stepKey` (lines 99–102) keys a step by the label before ' — ', or the whole title, so a renumbered title is a new key; and `reconcileEntry` (lines 253–279) treats an unknown key in a slot whose old key the plan no longer has as the same step retitled (lines 266–267), which hands the whole state to whatever now stands there. 57 step titles on memoro's main today start with a number and a period.

Add above `stepKey`: `/** A key without a leading ordinal: `5. The close`, `8) The close` and `Step 3: The close` are `The close`. A planning session renumbers steps when it inserts some, and the state has to follow the step. */ export function keyOf(label) { const text = typeof label === 'string' ? label.trim() : ''; return text.replace(/^(?:step\s+)?\d+[.:)]\s+/iu, '').trim() || null; }`. `stepKey` becomes `const title = …; return keyOf(title.split(/\s+[—–-]\s+/u)[0]);`. `W4.1.2` and `1.2 thing` are unchanged (the ordinal needs punctuation followed by whitespace).

In `reconcileEntry`: the `keyed` map (line 257) becomes `entry.steps.map((state, index) => { if (!state.key) return { ...state, key: keys[index] ?? null }; const key = keyOf(state.key); return key === state.key ? state : { ...state, key }; })`, so an entry written with `5. The close` reads as `The close` and is written once with the new key; an entry whose keys are already clean keeps its objects and `changed` stays false. Add `const carried = [];`. The fallback (line 267) becomes: `if (here && !wanted.has(here.key)) { carried.push({ index, from: here.key, to: keys[index] }); return { ...here, key: keys[index], stacked_on: null, red: null, interrupted: null, ...(here.status === 'done' ? {} : { pr: null, branch: null, attempts: 0 }), comments: [...(here.comments || []), `Carried by position on ${now ?? 'an unknown time'} from '${here.key}': a re-plan put '${keys[index]}' in this slot, so its status stays (Martin, 2026-10-03) and the pull request fields of the step it replaced are cleared.`] }; }`. Status, `blocked_by`, `reason` and `landed` stay. Return `{ entry, changed, carried }` from both returns (the running-step early return gives `carried: []`). `overlayPlans` (line 405) ignores `carried` for now; step 6 logs it. Rewrite the doc comment above `reconcileEntry` (lines 234–252): keys ignore a leading ordinal; an unknown key in a slot whose old key is gone keeps that slot's status, per Martin's ruling of 2026-10-03 that a re-planned blocked step is not released, but not its pull request, branch, stack or red, which were another step's (photo-viewer, #13580, 2026-10-12).

Tests in `tests/mc/register.test.js`. Extend 'stepKey is the label a title opens with, or the whole title' (line 156): `stepKey({ title: '8. The close' })` is `'The close'`; `'5) The close'` → `'The close'`; `'Step 3: Wire it — the rest'` → `'Wire it'`; `'1.2 thing'` → `'1.2 thing'`; and `keyOf('5. The close')` is `'The close'`. steps.title: Every register write appends one line to runner/log/register.log naming the process
steps.done_when: `updateStep` and `overlayPlans` in `src/mc/register.js` append one JSON line per write to `~/mc/runner/log/register.log` with `at`, `project`, the event, the step and `by` (`pid`, `ppid`, `parent`, `run`, `argv`, `cwd`, `mc_step`), never throwing; the new tests in `tests/mc/register.test.js` pass; `mc gate` is green.
instruction: Why: on 2026-10-12 `log-page` step 1, landed at 06:28Z as memoro #13590, stood `ready` again that evening, and the runner ran it twice for nothing (18:36Z and 20:24Z). The register keeps no history (`emptyStep`, `src/mc/register.js` line 86), and `~/mc/runner/projects/log-page.json` is gone: `mc tidy` deletes an archived project's register file (`src/mc/tidy.js` around lines 431–436). The answer survived only in `~/.memoro/mc/logs/mc.log`, which records every invocation (`mc.start`, `src/mc-cli.js` line 40): `mc step ready log-page 1` at 17:45:48Z and again at 20:04:46Z, typed in `/Users/martinforsberg/memoro` by holder `martinforsberg@MacBookAir`, not an mc session, one minute after the decision for step 2 was answered; `mc step ready log-page 2` followed at 20:36:21Z. mc.log rotates at 8 MB into one `.1` (`rotateIfLarge`, `src/mc/logger.js` line 174), about three days a file, so it held by luck, and it records no parent process, so a person and a non-mc session look the same. A line per register write, in a file tidy does not delete, makes the next such move answerable.

In `src/mc/register.js`: import `appendFileSync`, `mkdirSync` and `spawnSync`; import `invocationShape`, `rotateIfLarge` and `runId` from `./logger.js`. Add `export function registerLogPath(root) { return join(root, 'runner', 'log', 'register.log'); }` and `export const REGISTER_LOG_MAX_BYTES = 4 * 1024 * 1024;`. Add `let parentSeen;` and `function parentName() { if (parentSeen !== undefined) return parentSeen; try { const r = spawnSync('ps', ['-o', 'comm=', '-p', String(process.ppid)], { encoding: 'utf8', timeout: 2000 }); parentSeen = r.status === 0 ? String(r.stdout || '').trim() || null : null; } catch { parentSeen = null; } return parentSeen; }` and `export function whoAmI() { return { pid: process.pid, ppid: process.ppid, parent: parentName(), run: runId(), argv: invocationShape(process.argv.slice(2)), cwd: process.cwd(), mc_step: process.env.MC_STEP || null }; }`. Add `const realAppend = (path, line) => { mkdirSync(dirname(path), { recursive: true }); rotateIfLarge(path, REGISTER_LOG_MAX_BYTES); appendFileSync(path, line, { mode: 0o644 }); };` (import `dirname`) and `function logWrite(root, append, by, fields) { try { append(registerLogPath(root), `${JSON.stringify({ at: new Date().toISOString(), ...fields, by: by() })}\n`); } catch { /* the log never fails the write */ } }`. `invocationShape` already keeps flag names and drops their values and free text, so no `--reason` text reaches the file.

`updateStep` (line 418) takes `append = realAppend, by = whoAmI`. Inside the lock, after `write(…)`: `const was = entry.steps[index]; const now2 = next.steps[index]; logWrite(root, append, by, { event: 'step', project, index, key: now2.key, from: was.status, to: now2.status, pr: now2.pr ?? null, fields: Object.keys(patch) });`. Every transition goes through `updateStep`: `mc step` (`src/mc/commands/step.js` line 149), the runner (`recordStep`, `src/mc/run.js` line 723, and line 2912), `step-release.js` line 171, the merger (`src/mc/merger.js` lines 200, 579, 586) and `mc merge`'s booking (`src/mc/commands/merge.js` line 87 and `bookDocsLanding`). `overlayPlans` (line 396) takes `append = realAppend, by = whoAmI` too: after seeding (line 403) `logWrite(root, append, by, { event: 'seed', project: record.project, steps: entry.steps.length, statuses: entry.steps.map((s) => s.status) })`; after a reconcile that changed something (line 406) `logWrite(root, append, by, { event: 'reconcile', project: record.project, carried: brought.carried || [] })`, using the `carried` list step 5 added. Update the doc comments of `updateStep` and `overlayPlans` with one sentence each, and the file's header comment with one paragraph naming `register.log` and the log-page case.

`mc tidy` must keep the file: its per-project rule is `sessionLogRe` (`src/mc/tidy.js` line 108), `<project>-<yyyymmddThhmmssZ>.{jsonl,json,json.err}`, which `register.log` does not match. Add one assertion to its tests instead of code: in `tests/mc/tidy.test.js` (find the `sessionLogRe` test), `sessionLogRe('register').test('register.log')` is false.

Tests in `tests/mc/register.test.js`, with `disk()` and `record`. (1) 'updateStep appends one line naming the process': `const lines = []; const append = (path, line) => lines.push([path, line]);` seed and write an entry with step 0 `done` via `overlayPlans([record([step(), step()])], { root: '/w', ...io, append, by: () => ({ pid: 7, ppid: 6, parent: 'zsh', run: 'run_x', argv: { verb: 'step', sub: 'ready' }, cwd: '/home/m/memoro', mc_step: null }) })` and `updateStep({ root: '/w', project: 'p', index: 0, patch: { status: 'done', pr: 3 }, …same append and by })`, then `updateStep(… patch: { status: 'ready' } …)`; the last line's path is `registerLogPath('/w')`, and `JSON.parse` of it has `event` 'step', `project` 'p', `index` 0, `from` 'done', `to` 'ready', `fields` `['status']`, `by.parent` 'zsh', `by.argv.sub` 'ready'; the first line has `event` 'seed' and `statuses` `['ready', 'ready']`. (2) 'a log that cannot be written never fails the write': `append: () => { throw new Error('disk full'); }`; `updateStep` returns the entry and the register file holds the new status. (3) 'whoAmI names this process': `whoAmI().pid` is `process.pid`, `.ppid` is `process.ppid`, `.run` matches `/^run_/u`, `.argv` is an object. (4) 'a re-plan that carries a slot is logged with what it carried': after step 5's carry case (`[titled('A'), titled('B')]` → `[titled('A'), titled('Z')]`) through `overlayPlans` with `append`, the last line has `event` 'reconcile' and `carried` `[{ index: 1, from: 'B', to: 'Z' }]`.

Docs: `docs/technical/mc-run.md` § *The register*: one paragraph saying every register write appends a JSON line to `~/mc/runner/log/register.log` — what changed and which process did it (pid, parent process, run id, argument shape, directory, `MC_STEP`), rotated at 4 MB and kept by `mc tidy` — because on 2026-10-12 a hand-typed `mc step ready log-page 1` moved a landed step back to `ready` and the register that could have said so was tidied away with its project. Changelog: `changelog.d/register-log.md`, `section: Added`.

`mc gate tests/mc/register.test.js tests/mc/tidy.test.js`, then `mc gate`, `mc publish`, `mc merge memoro-cli <pr>`. This is the plan's last step: in the same PR set every `success_criteria[].met` in this plan to true.
